question: Which pioneer scientist used radio waves to transmit signals over distances of several kilometres in the 1890s?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Guglielmo Marconi.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Guglielmo Marconi** was an** Italian inventor and electrical engineer.**
 
• He conducted pioneering work in **long-distance radio transmission.**
 
• Marconi developed a practical **radio wave-based wireless telegraph system** in the late** 19th century.**
 
• His system was able to transmit signals over distances of **several kilometers.**
 
• Marconi's contributions helped significantly expand the field of** telecommunications.**
 
• His work was recognized internationally when he was awarded the** Nobel Prize for Physics in 1909.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Michael Faraday:**

 
 
• Michael Faraday was a** British scientist **who contributed significantly to the field of** electromagnetism and electrochemistry.**
 
• He discovered **electromagnetic induction, diamagnetism, and the laws of electrolysis.**
 
• Although Faraday **discovered electromagnetic fields**, he did not work on radio wave transmission.
 
 
 
• **Paul Langevin:**
 
 
• Paul Langevin was a **French physicist.**
 
• He is known for his work in developing **Langevin dynamics and the Langevin equation.**
 
• He developed the use of **ultrasound** using piezoelectricity but wasn't involved in radio wave transmission.
 
 
 
• **Pierre Weiss:**
 
 
• Pierre Weiss was a **French physicist** known for his work in** magnetism.**
 
• He introduced the concept of magnetic domains, which helps explain the magnetic behavior in **ferromagnetic materials.**
 
• His main work was on magnetism, not on radio wave transmission.
